records.title: Mediation and soft spectra after stabilization
records.question: How do stabilization choices determine mediation strengths and soft spectra, and when must supersymmetry-breaking matter and compactification moduli be stabilized together?

records.title: Sequestering and hidden–visible flavor transmission
records.question: When do compactification moduli, distant stabilization effects or hidden-sector expectation values transmit flavor-sensitive interactions, and when can warping suppress them?

records.title: Does stabilization require small flux W0?
records.question: Do EFT consistency, phenomenology or vacuum statistics require hierarchically small type IIB W0, or can values of order 1–10 remain consistent after stabilization?

records.title: Soft terms from stabilized moduli
records.question: How do stabilization, localization and effective couplings determine visible soft terms and the relative strengths of mediation channels?

records.title: Sequestering, bulk exchange and flavor
records.question: Under what conditions do brane separation or local compactification structure suppress unwanted soft terms and flavor violation, and when do bulk couplings obstruct that suppression?

records.title: Mediation, spectra and gauge relations
records.question: Which supersymmetry-breaking transmission patterns, soft terms, mass hierarchies and gauge-coupling relations follow from a specified stabilized model?

records.title: PQ-preserving saxion stabilization
records.question: Can uplift stabilize the saxion while preserving the QCD axion direction until QCD effects, and what spectrum and mediation follow?

records.title: Supersymmetry breaking and visible-sector masses
records.question: How do stabilization and its corrections affect sequestering, mediation, gravitino–gaugino hierarchies and visible-sector soft terms?

pilotNeighborhoods.proposal: Compare three repeated control scopes for shared target/reuse; keep solution existence, positive stationarity, retained-sector stability, statistical rarity and hierarchy tests distinct.
changedPremiseContrasts: A positive stationary scalar potential is not a complete higher-dimensional solution.
Necessary selected-sector stability conditions do not prove full metastability.
Vacuum-population multiplicity/distributions and conditional random-Hessian search probabilities are different statistical objects.
Finite control and controlled asymptotic families require distinct premises.
The lightest nonzero moduli mass is not automatically the Kaluza–Klein gap.

records.title: Existence and compactification ingredients
records.question: Which ingredients, internal geometries and source configurations permit de Sitter solutions in each stated theory and dimension?

records.title: String consistency and control
records.question: Can a proposed solution satisfy correction suppression, discrete consistency conditions and the claimed scale hierarchy, either at a finite point or parametrically?

records.title: Positive extrema and conditional no-go results
records.question: Which compactification ingredients and background restrictions permit or exclude positive stationary scalar potentials?

records.title: Control and string consistency
records.question: Under what source-specific conditions do compactification candidates satisfy quantization, source consistency and effective-theory control requirements?

records.title: Control, consistency and asymptotic families
records.question: When does a proposed compactification remain consistent and quantitatively controlled at finite parameters or along an asymptotic family?

records.title: Vacuum multiplicity, distributions and predictivity
records.question: How do specified compactification models populate vacuum space, and what can their distributions or multiplicities establish?

records.title: Statistical rarity and uplift-induced mixing
records.question: Under the stated random-Hessian approximations, how rare are tachyon-free Type IIA de Sitter extrema, and how does increasing vacuum energy affect stability through moduli mixing?

records.title: Necessary existence and selected-sector stability conditions
records.question: Which classical type-II compactifications survive necessary de Sitter existence and selected-sector stability tests when source arrangements and spacetime dimension are kept explicit?

records.title: Potential bounds and hierarchy tests
records.question: Are proposed potential inequalities and restrictions on scale separation compatible with the particular compactifications and effective actions used to test them?

sourceWitnesses.description: Can stabilizing a visible-sector singlet in a KKLT-motivated effective theory produce gauge mediation comparable to modulus and anomaly mediation, and how do messenger thresholds change soft terms and low-energy spectra?
sourceWitnesses.note: Compound mediator-stabilization and threshold-spectrum targets; comparable mediation differs from gauge dominance.

sourceWitnesses.description: When do geometrically distant moduli-stabilising effects or hidden scalar vevs induce visible-sector Yukawa couplings with new flavour structure, undermining sequestering and contributing to flavour violation?

Can type IIB compactifications suppress flavor-violating hidden–visible supersymmetry-breaking couplings despite compactification moduli, and can strong warping provide robust sequestering suitable for flavor-blind mediation?

Can gauge-mediated SUSY breaking dominate in a type IIB model with stabilized moduli and tuned vacuum energy, and can the SUSY-breaking matter sector consistently be treated independently of nonperturbatively stabilized Kähler moduli?
sourceWitnesses.note: Gauge dominance and matter–modulus independence are distinct tests; joint stabilization is the source's conclusion in its analyzed framework.

sourceWitnesses.description: Does physically separating visible matter and supersymmetry breaking on different branes enforce a sequestered Kähler potential, suppress tree-level scalar masses, and make anomaly mediation a generic solution to the supersymmetric flavor problem?
sourceWitnesses.note: The analyzed backgrounds have nonsequestered couplings and generally nonuniversal tree-level masses. This rejects separation alone as a guarantee.

sourceWitnesses.description: Do known stabilization mechanisms generically leave bulk fields parametrically below the Kaluza–Klein scale in supersymmetric string compactifications, obstructing the suppression of bulk exchange sought in anomaly and gaugino mediation?
sourceWitnesses.note: Known large-radius stabilization effects motivate the mass bound; asymmetric radii and specially constrained couplings prevent a universal mediation no-go.

sourceWitnesses.description: Can a PQ-invariant generalization of KKLT stabilize the saxion while leaving the QCD axion unfixed until QCD effects arise, and what moduli spectrum, supersymmetry-breaking mediation, and flavor/CP properties follow?
sourceWitnesses.note: Compound PQ-preserving stabilization and phenomenology. The tachyon concerns the pre-uplift phase; its suggested exclusionary interpretation remains historical.

sourceWitnesses.description: How do KKLT and LVS stabilize type IIB moduli, and what consequences follow for supersymmetry breaking, low-energy phenomenology, inflation, destabilization and moduli backreaction?
sourceWitnesses.note: The review spans stabilization, phenomenology and inflation without one resolved fine question. Its unfavorable spectrum assessment remains source-dated.

sourceWitnesses.description: Does sequestering by geometric separation or strong warping survive nonperturbative stabilization of Kähler moduli, and what soft terms follow in KKLT and Large Volume Scenario compactifications?
How do KKLT and LVS stabilize type IIB moduli, and what consequences follow for supersymmetry breaking, low-energy phenomenology, inflation, destabilization and moduli backreaction?
sourceWitnesses.note: Fine identity remains unresolved: the survey bundles mechanisms, particle phenomenology, inflation, destabilization and backreaction.

sourceWitnesses.description: Which tensor weak coupling limits are available in Type IIB/K3, and which can be described entirely by Kähler geometry at fixed complex structure?
sourceWitnesses.note: Tensor weak coupling supplies an alternate geometric-limit question without establishing a stabilization mechanism.

sourceWitnesses.description: Can gauge-mediated SUSY breaking dominate in a type IIB model with stabilized moduli and tuned vacuum energy, and can the SUSY-breaking matter sector consistently be treated independently of nonperturbatively stabilized Kähler moduli?
sourceWitnesses.note: Gauge-mediation dominance and matter-sector independence are separate linked tests, with tuned vacuum energy a stated requirement.

sourceWitnesses.description: Do integrated trace-reversed ten-dimensional Einstein equations obstruct KKLT de Sitter uplift once D7 gaugino condensation, its volume dependence, and a strongly warped positive-tension uplift source are treated consistently?
How does the same fixed-volume K3 degeneration differ when the reduced bulk potential is a one-form coupled to wrapped-M2 particles rather than a two-form coupled to wrapped-D3 strings?
sourceWitnesses.note: The setting-derived comparison supplies no antibrane-uplift target.

sourceWitnesses.description: Does a controlled string compactification admit metastable de Sitter space or an AdS vacuum whose lightest nonzero moduli mass is parametrically above the curvature scale?
sourceWitnesses.note: Compound dS and AdS targets. The effective-action example remains conditional; o26's formula/image addendum and o27's phase reconstruction are unverified object
